name: King Arthur
note: There is no Arthur to read. He left no writing, and the earliest mentions — a line in the Historia Brittonum, an entry in the Annales Cambriae — are a sentence each and centuries after any life he might have had. So this is not an author's shelf but the tradition that built him: the chronicle that invented his reign, the Welsh tales that remember someone older and rougher, and the romance that fixed him in English. Read in that order and you can watch a figure being assembled. Nennius and Gildas are not here yet — they need a public-domain translation confirmed rather than the first one a search returns.

works.title: Histories of the Kings of Britain (Historia Regum Britanniae)
works.source: Geoffrey of Monmouth · tr. Sebastian Evans, 1904 · Internet Sacred Text Archive · public domain
works.note: Where Arthur becomes a king rather than a name in a list — Uther for a father, Merlin, a war against Rome, a wound carried to Avalon. Geoffrey claims an ancient book as his source and no one has found it since. Note what is NOT here: no Round Table, no Grail, no Lancelot, no sword from a lake. Those arrive later.
